root.name: Vienna Gambit, with Max Lange Defense: Hamppe-Muzio Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. f4 exf4 4. Nf3 g5 5. Bc4 g4 6. O-O gxf3

overview: White has sacrificed a knight on f3 after the Hamppe-Muzio: Black has pawns on f4 and a knight on f3 and White plays Qxf3 with a direct attack on f7 and the f-file. White gets a big lead in development and open lines at the cost of a full piece. Black can often keep the material and defend, but it is dangerous in practice.

white_ideas.idea: Recapture with Qxf3 and open lines against f7
Bring the pieces out with d3, Nd5 and Bxf4
Attack the king with Qf3, Bc4 and Rxf4

black_ideas.idea: Keep the piece and defend with ...Qe7 and ...Nf6
Return material at the right moment to untangle
Trade queens and use the extra piece in the endgame

typical_structures.structure: Open centre and open f-file, White a piece down

character.notes: A piece sacrificed for a direct attack leaves the game forcing.

gambit.notes: Black can keep the knight after ...gxf3 if defending accurately.

soundness.notes: Theory regards the Muzio as unsound but practically dangerous.

approach.notes: Seldom played by strong players, who prefer other Vienna lines.

level.notes: White must know the attacking lines to get the compensation.

character.reason: A piece is sacrificed for a direct attack.

gambit.reason: White has given a knight that Black can keep.

soundness.reason: The Muzio is considered unsound but hard to refute over the board.

structure.reason: The f-file, e-file and diagonals are open.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom play the Muzio idea in the Vienna.

level.reason: It is dubious so not Beginner, and relies on specific lines.

plans.reason: White plays for the attack on f7 and the king.
